_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run cases (npm run check:golden pep). Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200, no truncation. V2 REWRITE (2026-09-05): the entire tool was rebuilt to remove a fabricated measurement system that the old pep-v1 golden's own captured output demonstrates (energy_read/pleasure_vs_numbing language, nervous-system claims, quick_hits/medium_recharge/deep_reset categories, battery percentages, introvert/extrovert energy types, task-cost arithmetic, burnout-risk radar, and a debt-check 'prescription' action) — none of that exists in v2. DO NOT reintroduce it while chasing a golden diff. New schema per mode: generate={read,top_pick,other_options,from_your_history} (was energy_read/mood_note/time_note/transition_tip/pleasure_vs_numbing/menu.quick_hits+medium+deep+avoid); budget={read,protect,consider_next,postpone_or_drop,sequence,one_decision} (was capacity_status/total_cost/available/permissions/tomorrow_note — no more summing task 'cost' as literal arithmetic); forecast={week_shape,demanding_stretches,breathing_room,commitments_to_reconsider,from_your_history,one_move_now} (was current_battery/recharge_hours/introvert-extrovert drain multipliers — inputs are now demanding_factors checkboxes + starting_capacity, not an energy_type slider); disruption={situation,keep,lighten,pause,temporary_shape,unknowns,reassess_when,one_next_step} (was acknowledgment/survival_schedule/self_care_minimum — critically, disruption with a BLANK normal_routine must not invent a generic exercise/meal/hygiene/medication/sleep routine; it must list the gap under 'unknowns' instead, which the adapt-sick-day-sparse-input case exists specifically to guard). radar-checkin and radar-analyze (Patterns) now share ONE schema shape ({today,what_changed,possible_patterns,not_enough_to_tell,worth_watching,optional_next_step}) instead of radar-checkin's old ad hoc fields vs radar-analyze's separate overall_risk/time_until_concern/interventions shape — no green/yellow/orange/red status, no 'time until burnout' estimate. debt-check action REMOVED ENTIRELY (was prescription/debt_level/gentle_warning — all now-banned terms). Wire field names productivity/social_energy/physical_symptoms on radar-checkin/radar-analyze are DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED from v1 despite the UI relabeling 'Productivity' to 'Focus / getting things done' — preserves existing users' checkinLog history; do not rename these on a future pass without a migration. activityLog client-side cap raised from 6 to 100 (PF-25 exception, see src/tools/PEP.js). menu items no longer store category/effort/avg_rating/use_count/sensory_anchor — My Menu now computes timesTried/avgRating/energy ranges fresh from activityLog on every render (menuStats()), so a stale-cache class of bug is structurally gone. DO NOT reverse: the removal of battery/introvert-extrovert/burnout-radar/debt-check language; the disruption blank-routine guard; the unified Patterns schema; the productivity/social_energy field name preservation; the fresh-computed (not stored) menu stats. RIGHT NOW FINAL CORRECTIONS pass (2026-09-05, same day): fixed an invented-clock-time bug (time_of_day='Evening' but the read stated a specific hour like '3pm' that was never supplied — now relative timing only unless the visitor's own text names an exact time); added an effort-absolutes ban ('zero setup/effort/decisions', 'no attention', 'completely passive' → 'very little' instead); banned internal-effect explanations standing in for a fit explanation ('fills the window without demanding attention'); and reinforced that a saved-menu item is preference evidence only, never promoted to 'likely to recharge you' or 'your best recovery tool' without actual prior ratings. Three new validateResult() regex categories added for these (unsupported absolute about effort / internal-effect claim / saved-menu oversold). The 'right-now-evening-no-clock-time-with-saved-menu' case exists specifically to guard the clock-time regression — DO NOT let a future edit reintroduce an invented specific hour when only a period of day (morning/afternoon/evening) was supplied.

input.context: Been staring at screens all day, doom-scrolling between meetings. A hike sounds awful right now.

output.read: You've reported energy at 2/10, a numb mood, and a full day of screen time — so the conditions point toward something that asks very little of you and doesn't add more screen exposure.

top_pick.activity: Sit somewhere away from your screens with a drink and do nothing in particular.
top_pick.why_it_fits: It asks nothing of you — no setup, no task, no screen — and fits inside your 15 minutes with no transitions required beyond moving from where you are.
top_pick.first_step: Put your phone face-down, go to a different seat or room, and make or grab something to drink.
top_pick.duration: However long feels right inside the 15 minutes.
top_pick.done_when: When the 15 minutes are up, or whenever you feel like moving on.

other_options.activity: Put on music or a podcast with your eyes closed.
other_options.why_it_fits: Low-demand listening without a screen matches your stated constraint around screens and fits easily inside 15 minutes at home.
other_options.duration: One song or a short podcast segment — 5 to 15 minutes.

other_options.activity: Step outside briefly — even just onto a doorstep or balcony.
other_options.why_it_fits: You noted a hike sounds awful, but a few minutes outside with no destination is a different scale of demand entirely — very short, no gear, no plan needed.

output.read: You've rated your capacity at 3/10 and you're stressed, while your one required task is your most demanding item. That gap is worth acknowledging before deciding how to spend what you have.

protect.why: You marked it required, so I'd protect time for it unless you know it can move.
protect.make_it_easier: Rather than finishing it in one sitting, decide the smallest version of 'done' that satisfies the actual deadline — a complete draft, a specific section, or hitting send on what exists. Starting with one defined piece may be more workable than approaching the whole thing at once.

consider_next: Reply to 40 emails — if you do this at all today, consider whether you can reply to fewer: the ones that are actually time-sensitive, rather than all 40.

postpone_or_drop.reason: Optional, and doing it now adds demand on top of your required task without a clear payoff today.
Optional and higher demand than most of your other tasks. Nothing here suggests today is the right day to stack it in.

sequence: Quarterly report first — while your capacity is at its highest point of the day, whatever that is.
If something is left afterward and you want to use it, a reduced version of the email task.
output.one_decision: Define what 'finish' actually means for the quarterly report today — a specific, bounded output — so you know exactly what you are protecting capacity for.

The big presentation falls the morning after the longest day of the week, with no buffer between Wednesday evening and a 10am start. You identified hosting or leading as especially demanding, and presenting is a form of leading.

breathing_room.option: You mentioned a quiet evening the night before helps around busy days. Tuesday night is the evening before Wednesday's packed schedule — keeping it unscheduled or low-key is an option worth protecting.
These days appear unscheduled based on what you entered. Moving any flexible tasks or preparation work into these days could reduce what you are carrying into Wednesday.

commitments_to_reconsider: The client dinner on Wednesday evening — you marked it as cannot leave early, but if there is any flexibility on whether to attend at all, it sits at the most compressed point of your week. Worth confirming whether attendance is truly required.
